newsitem.title: USA: US EPA air plan would put big cost on refiners - API.
newsitem.headline: US EPA air plan would put big cost on refiners - API.

text.p: Proposed stricter U.S. air quality standards would burden refiners that are not equipped to produce the large amount of reformulated gasoline the rule would require, the American Petroleum Institute's president said Tuesday.

The Environmental Protection Agency's proposed stricter standards against pollution from smog and air particles that may damage lungs would greatly increase the amount of RFG that areas would have to use to meet standards, API president Charles DiBona said.
"As you increase the volume, you go to refineries that are harder and harder to modify, and therefore the marginal costs will rise, and therefore the price will rise," DiBona said in a news briefing.
DiBona said the industry produces about 25 percent of the nation's gasoline as RFG and has the capacity to produce about 33 percent.
"There may be some capacity above 25 percent, but it's not 50," DiBona said.
He said the industry's 5-cents per gallon premium estimate for RFG was based on a 33 percent marketshare. But he said costs would rise as more refineries would have to retool.
